memos.headline: S09 at 52-week highs and S06 near highs lead the tape; S01 and S04 in confirmed downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in the universe as we start 2026. S09 is printing a fresh 52-week high (zero drawdown) with RSI 65 and positive 4w relative strength of +4.2% vs SPY — textbook trend continuation. S06 sits just -1.1% off its high with strong 4w rel strength of +4.4% and a low-volatility ATR of 1.40%, making it the cleanest uptrend in the group. On the other side, S01 is -19.6% off its 52-week high, trading 9.1% below its 200-day mean with an RSI of 40.9 and 12w rel strength of -9.1% vs SPY — a broken trend I want no part of. S04 shows similar weakness at RSI 37.3, -12.8% drawdown, and -11.8% 12w relative strength, though it is closer to its 200d mean (-1.1%) so a bounce is possible but I would not chase it. S05 and S07 have monster 26w returns (+76.5% and +55.5%) and remain well above their 200d means, but the extreme extension (S05 is +44.5% above 200d) raises mean-reversion risk; I am cautiously constructive but would tighten stops on any break below the 50d average.

views.note: At 52-week high with strong 4w and 12w relative strength; would reassess on a close below 117.50 (roughly the 50d area).
Only -1.1% from highs, RSI 59.5, best 4w rel strength in the group at +4.4%; invalidated below 310 (~50d zone).
Massive 12w +23% move with +20.9% rel strength, but +37.3% above 200d is stretched; a close below 570 would flip me neutral.
Strongest 26w return at +76.5% but +44.5% above 200d is the most extended name in the universe; risk/reward less attractive here.

The -43.9% drawdown from 52w high is alarming despite a recent bounce; trading below 200d mean and 12w rel strength is -9.6%.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a stark divergence in durable earnings quality across this universe. S10 stands out with 56% net margins, +62.5% YoY revenue growth, and only $8.47B in total debt—this is the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S05 also impresses at 34.2% net margins on $102.35B revenue with +33% YoY net income growth and minimal leverage ($14.79B debt). On the other end, S02's net margin has collapsed to 2.1% with net income down 61.2% YoY despite 12.2% revenue growth—classic margin compression I refuse to pay for. S09 is shrinking (-5.2% revenue, -12.3% net income) with an 8.8% margin and $32.82B in debt, which is a deteriorating profile. I would need to see margin stabilization in S02 and a return to revenue growth in S09 before reconsidering either name.

views.note: 56% net margin, 62.5% YoY revenue growth, and near-zero leverage ($8.47B debt) represent the strongest earnings power in the universe.
34.2% net margin with +33% YoY net income growth and low debt of $14.79B signals durable, high-quality earnings.
35.7% net margin on $77.67B revenue with +18.4% YoY revenue growth and manageable $43.21B debt is a strong profile, though net income growth of 12.5% lags revenue growth slightly.
Net income surged 86.4% YoY to $27.47B but $90.68B in total debt and only 7.9% revenue growth suggest the earnings jump may not be fully sustainable without continued margin expansion.
Revenue of $180.17B (+13.4% YoY) is massive but 11.8% net margin and $55.10B debt leave limited room for error; I need to see margin expansion to get constructive.
31% net margin is attractive but $427.20B in total debt dwarfs the rest of the universe and makes earnings highly sensitive to funding costs.
21.2% net margin and +20% YoY net income growth are solid, but only 3% revenue growth on $22.39B suggests limited top-line momentum.
13% net margin with declining net income (-6.7% YoY) and $31.74B debt on only $17.64B revenue warrants caution until earnings stabilize.

Net margin collapsed to 2.1% and net income fell 61.2% YoY despite 12.2% revenue growth—this is textbook cash-flow compression with $80.14B in debt amplifying the risk.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Softening Labor Market and Sticky CPI Argue for a Late-Cycle Defensive Tilt
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound has fallen 75 bp over the past year to 3.75%, with 50 bp of that in the last three months alone, while the effective rate sits at 3.88% as of November. However, CPI is running at +2.7% y/y—still above target—and unemployment has crept up 30 bp over the year to 4.50%, signaling a softening but not collapsing labor market. The 10y-2y spread has steepened 38 bp y/y to +0.71 pp, which is constructive for banks and suggests the market is pricing in continued easing, yet the 10y yield at 4.19% has barely moved in three months (+9 bp), indicating the long end is anchored by inflation concerns. My regime call is 'easing into slowdown': I favor duration-sensitive growth and banks over cyclicals and energy, and would watch the next CPI print closely—a re-acceleration above 3% y/y would force me to downgrade growth-sensitive names and upgrade staples.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from ongoing Fed easing cycle with upper bound down 75 bp y/y and curve steepening.
Banks gain from a steeper yield curve (+38 bp y/y to 0.71 pp) which supports net interest margins in an easing regime.
Staples are a hedge if CPI re-accelerates above 3% y/y, but at 2.7% the inflation picture doesn't yet warrant a full defensive rotation.
Cyclicals face headwinds from rising unemployment (+0.30 y/y to 4.50%) signaling demand softening; not yet distressed enough to avoid outright.
Energy typically underperforms in a slowdown regime with rising unemployment and moderating demand; I stay away until labor data stabilizes.
Growth-oriented name should benefit from lower front-end rates and easing financial conditions as the Fed continues to cut.

memos.headline: Leadership Churn Dominates Late-2025 Filings; S10 Earnings Miss Stands Out as Only Concrete Negative Signal
memos.body: I see a wave of Departure/Appointment of Directors or Officers 8-Ks across S08, S06, S04, S01, S02, and S09 in the Nov-Dec window, which by itself is largely governance noise rather than a narrative shift—these filings are common around year-end board refreshes. The one clear negative sentiment event is S10's Q3/Q4 results filing on 2025-11-19 that triggered a -3.2% price drop the next day, suggesting the market repriced on disappointing operations. S02 is the most active filer with three 8-Ks in two weeks (Reg FD, bylaws amendment, officer change), which could signal either proactive governance or internal turbulence—I lean cautious until we see follow-through. S09 also filed three times in under a month including two 'Other Events' filings before a board change, a pattern that sometimes precedes strategic repositioning. Without GDELT tone data or media volume metrics, I am working purely off filing cadence and market reaction, so my confidence levels are modest across the board.

views.note: Earnings-related 8-K drew a -3.2% price reaction, indicating negative sentiment likely not fully washed out yet.
Three 8-Ks in two weeks (Reg FD, bylaws, officer change) suggest elevated corporate activity but direction is ambiguous.
Cluster of three filings including two Other Events before a board change hints at possible strategic shift, but no tone data to confirm.
Board change plus shareholder vote is routine governance; no sentiment signal either way.
Single Other Events filing with no price reaction data; insufficient to form a directional view.
Officer departure/appointment filing is standard year-end governance noise.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Spikes Into New Year While Oil Weakness Signals Muted Energy-Security Premium
memos.body: I note a divergence entering 2026: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index jumped 11.7% month-over-month to 288.09, yet the VIX fell to 14.95 (down 8.6% m/m) and HY spreads tightened 11bp to 2.81%, suggesting markets are complacent relative to the policy backdrop. WTI crude at $57.26 is down 9.4% over three months, which eases energy-security concerns but may reflect demand-side weakness or expectations of looser sanctions enforcement—either reading matters for energy-exposed names. The steepening yield curve (+15bp over 3m to 0.71pp on 10y-2y) is consistent with fiscal-policy uncertainty rather than imminent recession risk. I have limited visibility into specific sanctions or export-control actions from the 8-K filings for S03, S02, and S09, which disclosed only generic Other Events and Reg FD items without geopolitical detail, so my conviction on those names is low. A concrete policy trigger that would change my view would be new China export controls on semiconductors or an expansion of Russian energy sanctions—neither is evident in the data today.

views.note: No company-specific geopolitical signal; low oil prices reduce energy-cost headwinds but elevated policy uncertainty warrants caution.
8-K Other Events filing in November provides no actionable geopolitical content; staying sidelined until clarity emerges.
Reg FD disclosure offers no detail on supply-chain or sanctions exposure; policy uncertainty index rise keeps me cautious.
Two 8-K filings in November lack geopolitical specifics; absent new export-control or sanctions news, no directional call.
Falling oil prices and tight credit spreads favor domestically oriented names with limited geopolitical tail risk; would reverse on new sanctions escalation.
No direct geopolitical evidence; elevated policy uncertainty index argues against aggressive positioning despite benign VIX.
